title: Odile and the Vector
premise: Yara Amberdale has spent eleven years alone tending Earth's derelict seed vault, keeping its beacon lit for a fleet that never answers—until a distress signal arrives in a language extinct since the Meridian Massacre, an event every surviving record insists never happened. The signal's sender, a fugitive archivist named Odile Voss, carries the only proof of the atrocity: a memory vector that must reach the fleet's arbitration council before their truce expires in forty days. Pursued by a revisionist armada and betrayed by the beacon's true purpose—a lure built to erase witnesses like her—Yara must choose between the comfortable lie of his isolation and a truth that will cost him everything. In the end, Yara broadcasts Odile's vector through the very beacon meant to destroy it, forcing the fleet to confront its rewritten history as the truce collapses into open reckoning.
about_author: Beatrix Thackeray is a former radio astronomer who left observatory life to write fiction about the silences between signals. She lives on a decommissioned listening station off the coast of Norway, where she repairs antique transmitters and collects extinct alphabets.

chapters.title: The Keeper of Small Green Things
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Establishes his solitary routine inside the seed vault: cataloging seeds, maintaining the beacon, talking to the dormant cryo-gardens. Emotional beat: contentment shadowed by loneliness; he has convinced himself invisibility is peace.

chapters.title: A Signal in a Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The beacon intercepts a distress transmission in Old Meridian, a language wiped out two centuries ago. Yara, who learned it from forbidden archive fragments, translates enough to realize someone is alive and asking for sanctuary. Beat: wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Odile
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Introduces Odile Voss fleeing through debris fields in a crippled courier ship, carrying an encrypted memory vector she stole from the Revisionist Directorate. Flashbacks to the massacre she witnessed. Beat: desperate resolve.

chapters.title: Sanctuary Has a Price
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Odile crash-lands near the vault. Their first meeting is wary and hostile—she assumes he's Directorate bait; he fears she'll bring the war to his door. Beat: mutual suspicion giving way to grudging alliance.

chapters.title: What the Seeds Remember
chapters.summary: Dual POV alternating. Odile reveals the vector contains sensory recordings of the Meridian Massacre, expunged from all records. Yara recognizes vault logs his predecessor falsified. Beat: the ground shifting under Yara's identity as caretaker.

chapters.title: Forty Days
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The fleet's truce expires in forty days; after that, arbitration ends and the Revisionists can legally purge dissent. Odile lays out the plan: transmit the vector to the council before deadline. Beat: ticking clock established.

chapters.title: The Beacon's Second Voice
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Digging into the beacon's architecture, Yara discovers hidden hardware—it was never a lighthouse but a hunter-killer array designed to triangulate and erase memory-carriers like Odile. Beat: betrayal by the institution he served.

chapters.title: Ghost Fleet
chapters.summary: Revisionist Commander Hale's POV. The Directorate's pursuit squadron closes on Earth, led by rumors of a stolen vector. Hale privately doubts the official history. Beat: antagonist humanized; cracks in the lie.

chapters.title: Learning to Speak Again
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Quiet interlude: Odile teaches Yara the rest of Old Meridian; he shows her the living gardens. They grow close. Beat: tenderness amid danger, deepening stakes—if they fail, this dies too.

chapters.title: The Predecessor's Confession
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. In a sealed sub-vault, Yara finds his predecessor's suicide note confessing participation in the cover-up and leaving decryption keys. Beat: grief and fury; proof the massacre happened exists—but it's not enough without the vector.

chapters.title: First Contact, Wrong Kind
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A Directorate probe reaches the vault perimeter. Odile and Yara spoof the beacon to misdirect it, narrowly avoiding detection. Beat: first real danger; the clock accelerates.

chapters.title: Hale's Doubt
chapters.summary: Commander Hale's POV. Hale intercepts fragmentary transmissions in Old Meridian and secretly verifies them against sealed family records—his grandmother died at Meridian. Beat: antagonist begins covertly working both sides.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Directorate agents offer Yara amnesty and restoration of his records if he surrenders Odile. Tempted by the promise of his old identity back, he nearly accepts. Beat: loyalty vs. truth crystallized in one choice.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Yara rejects the offer and warns Odile, who had already packed to leave alone to spare him. A raw confrontation becomes a vow: they finish this together. Beat: love declared obliquely; commitment sealed.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The Directorate disables the vault's main transmitter remotely via the beacon's hidden array. With days left, their only option is to physically carry the vector to a relay station on the lunar far side. Beat: plan collapses; desperation rises.

chapters.title: The Long Dark Between
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The journey to Luna aboard a scavenged tug: radiation storms, failing life support, and Odile revealing the full horror of what she recorded. Beat: intimacy forged in extremity; the truth made flesh.

chapters.title: Relay Seven Falls
chapters.summary: Commander Hale's POV. The Directorate seizes Relay Seven ahead of them. Hale, now certain of the cover-up, quietly leaves a maintenance backdoor open—an act of treason he may not survive. Beat: the enemy becomes an uncertain ally.

chapters.title: Deadline Eve
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. They infiltrate Relay Seven through Hale's backdoor, but Odile is gravely wounded covering Yara's escape from a security sweep. The truce expires at dawn. Beat: climax pressure; sacrifice and terror.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Dual POV. At the relay's core, Yara uses the beacon's own hunter-killer array—inverted—to blast the vector fleet-wide, overriding the Directorate's jamming. Odile, bleeding out, recites the dead language aloud as it transmits. Beat: triumphant, costly climax.

chapters.title: The Reckoning
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Across the fleet, millions receive the massacre memories simultaneously. Arbitration councils convene mid-crisis; Hale testifies against the Directorate; revisionist command fractures. Beat: catharsis—the lie cannot hold.

chapters.title: After the Signal Fades
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Weeks later: Odile survives, recovering in the vault's medical bay. The fleet offers them both standing and titles; Yara asks instead for seeds, soil, and time. Beat: quiet resolution; identity rebuilt around truth rather than hiding.

chapters.title: What We Plant
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, closing mirror of chapter one. Together they reseed the first open garden and relight the beacon—now honestly a lighthouse, broadcasting the restored history of Meridian in its original tongue. Final beat: memory kept alive, chosen over forgetting.
